title: Presence Over Position
guide_title: Presence Over Position: Navigating Leadership and Humility
goal: Challenge men to prioritize presence with God over ambition for Earthly positions, integrating lessons from journeying through life's 'Badlands'.
scripture_instructions: Choose one or two men to read Mark 9:30-50 aloud. Let the group absorb the call to servant leadership and enduring faithfulness before discussion.

icebreakers.label: A
icebreakers.question: What was your first big leadership moment?

icebreakers.label: B
icebreakers.question: Tell us about a time when you thought you were in control but realized you weren't.

icebreakers.label: C
icebreakers.question: What's a 'Badlands' season you've navigated, and what did it teach you?

sections.title: Serve Without Agenda
sections.setup: In Mark 9, Jesus challenges His disciples' debates over greatness by placing a child, a symbol of humility and service, before them. Recognizing true greatness requires a redirection of ambition from self-serving to serving others.
sections.say: Jesus doesn't just compete for positions of power, he flips the script, calling us to serve without expectations.

questions.ask: Who in your life defines your concept of service without agenda?
questions.lead: Jesus used a child to illustrate ultimate humility and service.
questions.probe: How have they changed your approach to serving others?

questions.ask: When have you chosen a less visible role and found it fulfilling?
questions.lead: Our culture often equates greatness with visibility.
questions.probe: What made the experience rewarding given low visibility?

questions.ask: How do you treat people who hold no power over you?
questions.lead: A child in Jesus’ time had no legal standing.
questions.probe: What changes could you make to value them more intentionally?

questions.ask: Where do you still find yourself expecting something in return?
questions.lead: The preacher noted those sacrificial actions without expectation.
questions.probe: What changes in your heart when things are given freely?

reflection_questions: Who in my life defines my concept of service without agenda?
When have I chosen a less visible role and found it fulfilling?
How do I treat people who hold no power over me?
Where do I still find myself expecting something in return?

sections.title: Surrender the Impulse to be Territorial
sections.setup: The sermon outlined territorial behavior that limits God's work. Jesus rebukes the disciples for trying to control who can operate in His name, indicating a call for unity and cooperation within the church.
sections.say: The disciples tried to shut down others who weren't in their 'group'. Jesus corrected them, pointing toward a broader kingdom vision.

questions.ask: When have you put up walls around your faith?
questions.lead: John wanted to stop others from using Jesus' name.
questions.probe: What drove you to guard rather than share your faith?

questions.ask: Where are you holding control that needs release?
questions.lead: Territorial attitudes limit our vision of God’s work.
questions.probe: What patterns do you notice when you're protective?

questions.ask: Have you experienced unity bringing a breakthrough?
questions.lead: Jesus emphasized working together in unity.
questions.probe: What changed when you chose unity over division?

questions.ask: When have you experienced jealousy over someone else's role?
questions.lead: The disciples feared losing their position.
questions.probe: What was the underlying fear or insecurity?

reflection_questions: When have I put up walls around my faith?
Where am I holding control that needs release?
Have I experienced unity bringing a breakthrough?
When have I experienced jealousy over someone else's role?

sections.title: Avoid Sin, Stay Salty
sections.setup: Through hyperbolic language, Jesus illustrates the drastic measures sometimes necessary to avoid sin, emphasizing personal integrity and a life that influences others imperatively and positively.
sections.say: Jesus calls us to purity and impact, avoiding sin but seasoning life with godly characteristics.

questions.ask: Where are you tolerating a sin that needs to be addressed?
questions.lead: Cutting off sin is about drastic measures for purity.
questions.probe: What is the first small step you can take towards change?

questions.ask: How have you maintained or lost your Christian influence?
questions.lead: Jesus warned of losing saltiness, meaning influence.
questions.probe: What factors helped you stay or lose effectiveness as salt during life's challenges?

questions.ask: What prevents you from being a preservative in difficult environments?
questions.lead: Salt preserves, not just flavors our actions in society.
questions.probe: How can you lean more into showing up as a godly influence?

questions.ask: When have you ignored a warning and faced consequences?
questions.lead: Jesus talked about avoiding anything that leads us astray.
questions.probe: How could awareness lead to a better response in the future?

reflection_questions: Where am I tolerating a sin that needs to be addressed?
How have I maintained or lost my Christian influence?
What prevents me from being a preservative in difficult environments?
When have I ignored a warning and faced consequences?

closing_go_around: Go around and share one small action you’ll take this week to realign with God’s call to serve, unite, or be a positive influence.
prayer: Invite the group to pray for openness to find rest in God’s presence beyond the desire for strong positions or influences and trust in His timing.

cheat_sheet.response: Gently remind that not all issues are about personal failure; sometimes it's about letting God work.
Thank them for their story, then guide to a related discussion question.
Invite them directly with a light variation of one question. Engage personally without pressure.
Guide back with a specific action ask linked to the sermon applications.
Let them share, affirm their openness, then pray for them if the moment is right.

key_themes: Emphasize presence over position in our spiritual journey.
Genuine greatness is found in serving others selflessly.
Territorial impulses limit God's work; embrace unity.
Avoid sin passionately, illustrated through decisive, corrective action.
Live with kingdom influence, be salty and distinctive as Christ commands.
Personal and spiritual formation is prioritized over situation resolution.
Heeding the transformative lessons in life’s challenging 'Badlands'.
commitment_prompt: Pick one area you’ll trust God more with this week: serving, letting go of control, or purifying your actions, and share it with a partner.
thesis: God is more interested in the long-term formation of your soul than the short-term resolution of your circumstances.
sensitivities: Discussing badlands experiences may recall difficult personal trials for some men.
Emphasizing sin could trigger guilt or avoidance.
obstacle: Get honest about the control you might lose and fear when letting go of certain positions or habits.
carry: Next week, ask each other how the steps toward being salt and light went and what adjustments are ongoing.
